4Q83 f14i:35.en: For good is the loyalty from the living, their lips will praise
4Q83 f14i:35.notes: Uncertain reconstruction of 'lip' (position 6) and untranslatable character 'ε' (position 8) omitted from translation.

4Q83 f14ii:28.en: Go and hear and I will recount all afraid
4Q83 f14ii:28.notes: The transcription contains uncertain and reconstructed elements, including the first word and the final letter of 'שמעו['. The phrase 'כוליראי' is translated based on repeated phrase evidence as 'all afraid' rather than a literal gloss.

4Q83 f14ii:29.en: Gods which he made for my soul. To mouth I called and praise under my tongue. Wickedness if I saw in my heart not hears.
4Q83 f14ii:29.notes: The translation reflects the visible transcription and morphology, with uncertainty in the reconstruction of 'א##ל##הים[' and 'א ]ו#?ן'. The phrase 'to mouth' and '[are] under tongue' are supported by repeated phrase evidence. The sense of 'wickedness' for 'אָוֶן' is preferred over the town name due to contextual constraints. The final clause 'not hears' is a conservative rendering of the negated verb 'לוא ישמע', preserving the grammatical person and number.

4Q83 f14ii:30.en: My Lord, surely God heard and gave attention to the sound of my prayer. Blessed be the God who has not turned aside my prayer and loyalty.
4Q83 f14ii:30.notes: The transcription contains uncertain and reconstructed elements, including 'אכן?' and '[ הסיר'. The phrase 'ברוך אלהים' is translated based on repeated phrase evidence. The final '[ ו ]' is omitted as it cannot be translated independently.

4Q83 f14ii:31.notes: The final punctuation mark (׃) is omitted from the translation as it cannot be translated independently.

4Q83 f14ii:32.en: To prevail in music a psalm a song God may favour and bless make shine face sela to know in earth way
4Q83 f14ii:32.notes: Uncertain reconstruction of 'prevail' and 'bless'; phrase evidence supports 'choirmaster with stringed instruments' and 'God may'; 'sela' is a liturgical marker; 'face' is plural in the source but translated as singular due to contextual constraints.

4Q83 f14ii:33.en: In all the nations your salvation. Peoples O God may praise you with all. They will rejoice and cry out not to peoples.
4Q83 f14ii:33.notes: The translation follows the visible transcription and morphology. The phrase 'peoples O God may' is supported by repeated phrase evidence. Uncertainty in the final word is noted but not bracketed in the translation.

4Q83 f14ii:34.en: For you will judge peoples in fairness and nations on earth you will lead. Selah. And peoples O God may praise you, peoples.
4Q83 f14ii:34.notes: The translation follows the visible morphology and lexical glosses, with repeated phrase evidence guiding the rendering of 'peoples O God may' for positions 14-16. The lacuna at the beginning is preserved without brackets or placeholders. The translation conservatively retains all recoverable words in order, with no added subjects or connectors.

4Q83 f14ii:35.en: The land will give produce. He will bless us, God of gods. They will bless God and fear him, all the ends of the earth.
4Q83 f14ii:35.notes: Positions 2, 9, and 18 are untranslatable punctuation. Position 8 is uncertain due to damage.

4Q83 f19ii_20:25.en: To the choirmaster on lilies: David. Help me, God, for waters unto [the] neck have come. I sank in a depth; there is no position.
4Q83 f19ii_20:25.notes: Positions 3 and 13 are uncertain. Positions 1, 8, and 20 are reconstructed.

4Q83 f19ii_20:26.en: I came in the depths of waters, a stream washed me off. I was weary in calling, his throat was hoarse. His teeth were complete in labour pains to the God of Israel.
4Q83 f19ii_20:26.notes: Positions 6 and 12 have uncertain reconstructions. Positions 7 and 20 are untranslatable punctuation. Position 14's gloss is uncertain.

4Q83 f19ii_20:27.en: They were much from the hair of his head, my hating enemies in vain. They were mighty, silencing my foes, a lie that I did not tear away. Then I will return, God.
4Q83 f19ii_20:27.notes: The transcription is heavily damaged, with several reconstructed and uncertain words. The phrase 'the hair his head' is supported by repeated evidence. The translation conservatively follows the visible morphology and lexical glosses, preserving uncertainty and lacunae without adding speculative content.

4Q83 f19ii_20:28.en: You know, I did not accompany, and I will not be finished. Do not be ashamed, those who wait for the Lord, Yahweh of hosts, do not.
4Q83 f19ii_20:28.notes: The transcription contains significant damage and uncertainty, particularly in positions 6, 7, 8, 10, 12, and 13. The phrase 'I will not be finished' is a reconstruction based on the lemma and morphology of position 6. The word 'ε' (position 7) and the punctuation mark '׃' (position 8) are omitted from the translation due to lack of recoverable meaning. The phrase 'those who wait for the Lord, Yahweh of hosts, do not' is supported by repeated phrase evidence, but the exact connection to the preceding clause is uncertain.

4Q83 f19ii_20:29.en: They are humiliated who seek the God of Israel because I bore the reproach it has covered ignominy faces Who is a strange brother
4Q83 f19ii_20:29.notes: Uncertain reconstruction of damaged verbs at positions 1 and 16. Positions 10-11-12 use a repeated phrase with 100% support. Positions 3-4 use a repeated phrase with 90.4% support. Positions 16-17-18 use a repeated phrase with 20% support.

4Q83 f19ii_20:30.en: To the foreign sons of my mother: that jealousy ate and reproached my house, and those who spend autumn fell upon me. And only in fasting of soul
4Q83 f19ii_20:30.notes: Uncertain reconstruction of 'jealousy' (position 7), 'reproaches' (position 11), and 'fell' (position 13). Unclear meaning of 'spend autumn' (position 12). Incomplete text at the end.

4Q83 f19ii_20:31.en: To a reproach for me and I gave a garment and sack and it was to them as a proverb those who are concerned with the inhabitants of Seir
4Q83 f19ii_20:31.notes: The translation includes reconstructed and uncertain words. The phrase 'a reproach to' is supported by repeated phrase evidence. The phrase 'the inhabitants of Seir' is also supported by repeated phrase evidence. The verb 'play harp' is uncertain and omitted from the translation. The final verb 'drink' is uncertain and omitted from the translation.

4Q83 f19ii_20:32.en: Strong drink. And my prayer, why, YHWH, now the pleasure of God in the greatness of your covenant loyalty, answer me in trustworthiness of your help.
4Q83 f19ii_20:32.notes: The translation includes reconstructed and uncertain elements. The phrase 'in the greatness of your covenant loyalty' is supported by repeated phrase evidence. The word 'YHWH' is uncertain due to damage. The term 'god(s)' is reconstructed and uncertain. The final punctuation marks are omitted from the translation as they cannot be translated independently.

4Q83 f19ii_20:33.en: Deliver me from clay, and I will not sink. And let him take my plunder, deliver me from my enemies from the depths of water. Do not wash off
4Q83 f19ii_20:33.notes: Multiple uncertain and reconstructed words, including 'deliver' (נצל), 'sink' (טבע), 'plunder' (גזל), and 'wash off' (שׁטף). The translation follows visible morphology and lexical glosses, preserving grammatical structure and semantic relationships.

4Q83 f19ii_20:34.en: A grain of waters and not sink in the deep and not close upon the mouth of the well. Be lowly as good loyalty as great compassions.
4Q83 f19ii_20:34.notes: The translation reflects the visible morphology and phrase evidence, preserving uncertainty in the notes. The phrase 'as good loyalty' and 'as great compassions' are supported by dominant contextual renderings. Uncertainty in the transcription is noted for positions 2, 5, 6, 9, 11, and 19.

4Q83 f19ii_20:35.en: Turn to me do not hide your face from your servant that he will lay siege to me haste be lowly approach upon my soul redeem because of my enemies
4Q83 f19ii_20:35.notes: The phrase 'do not hide your face' is supported by repeated evidence. The sequence 'that he will lay siege to me' is a paraphrase based on repeated evidence. 'Haste' is uncertain due to damage. 'Be lowly' and 'approach' are imperative verbs. 'Upon my soul' and 'redeem' are supported by morphology. 'Because of my enemies' is a reconstruction.
